strategy.headline: Contrarian but not stupid: when an underdog is worth taking
strategy.summary: In a pick'em the favourite is usually the crowd's pick, so a correct underdog is what separates a leaderboard entry from the pack. The trade-off only pays when the underdog is backed by a verifiable reason and the price still leaves room. The rules below are project strategy, not verified outcomes.

rules.rule: Take the underdog when a roster change is recent and structural, not cosmetic.
rules.why: A new in-game leader, a new star and a new coach inside one split means an unproven system, new communication and a short practice window. Aurora's 2026 rebuild is the day-one example.
rules.verify: Official organisation announcements, the transfer timeline and the team's own statements, then confirm the current five on a fixture-specific source.

rules.rule: Take the underdog when the favourite is demonstrably fatigued and the market has not repriced.
rules.why: Deep runs plus travel compress preparation. A favourite whose price already fell has no contrarian value left.
rules.verify: Compare the favourite's recent tournament load and travel from results pages, then check whether the offered price still reflects the earlier reputation.

rules.rule: Prefer underdogs whose chance is roughly one in five or better, and expect to lose most of them.
rules.why: A 20-40% pick that wins is worth the same single point as a favourite but moves you past everyone who copied the crowd. Below that band the pick is a lottery ticket, not an edge.
rules.verify: Use the sourced market probability on the picks page. Where no market exists, use the labelled research tier and treat it as low confidence.

rules.rule: Never size up a contrarian pick on an identity or a number you cannot source.
rules.why: Renamed teams, academy squads and unclear aliases are exactly where a whole pick'em slips away on a wrong team.
rules.verify: The identity register in this project requires an exact opponent and UTC start before any alias is used.

rules.rule: Limit how many contrarian swings you take per slate.
rules.why: Stacking four underdogs multiplies variance instead of climbing the leaderboard.
rules.verify: Count the contrarian picks shown in the screen below; treat anything beyond one or two as exposure, not insight.

unverified: This project does not collect Hotspawn's pick'em scoring rules, so no claim is made about how many points a correct underdog is worth relative to a favourite.
No calibrated historical model exists here: contrarian picks are market-implied plus sourced context, and are not a promise of profit or of a higher leaderboard position.

day_three.headline: Day three: the two group deciders

market.label: Polymarket market 5733288 (Aurora Gaming vs 9z, event cs2-aur1-9z-2026-10-16)
market.detail: Raw prices 0.685 / 0.315 with best bid 0.68 and best ask 0.69 (1-point spread) and about $59.7k of liquidity when the refresh observed it at 22:32 UTC on 15 October 2026. The market description states the match was scheduled for 10:00 ET on 16 October 2026, which is the same 14:00 UTC slot the Hotspawn fixture carries.

points.claim: Aurora carry the ranking edge (#6 to #17) and a 3-of-5 recent win record, while 9z carry the head-to-head win and the momentum from taking a map off Falcons.
points.detail: HLTV analytics pros/cons for the decider, read 16 October 2026 (UTC).

points.claim: The external line makes Aurora a 68.5% favourite once the two-sided exchange quote is normalised, so 9z sit inside the project's 20-40% contrarian band: a pick that is contrarian but priced, not a lottery ticket.
points.detail: This is a market-implied probability recorded at a specific observation time and republished on the picks page; it is not a claim about the true chance of winning. See the live row for 1080205 in picks.html.

points.claim: Aurora have now played three LAN matches in about 30 hours, after arriving from a deep ESL Pro League Season 24 run in which they finished third.
points.detail: HLTV's day-one report describes Aurora's recent EPL S24 run and their 14 October defeat to 9z; the schedule load is a read of the published results, not a measured fatigue figure. A betting preview had raised fatigue as an opinion and is labelled as commentary elsewhere on this page.

contrarian.why: The framework only pays when an underdog has a verifiable reason and the price still leaves room. 9z beat this exact opponent 2-0 on 14 October, took a map off the tournament's strongest group winner, and are priced near 31.5%. Aurora are the better-ranked team and answered their critics on day two, which is the risk side of the trade.
not_stupid_check: Price still in the 20-40% band rather than a lottery ticket (rule 3).
The reason is a repeatable head-to-head result and a map win, not a rumour (rules 1 and 4).
Only one contrarian swing is in band on this slate, so exposure stays at one (rule 5).
contrarian.limits: This is analysis of a sourced market line, not a prediction. If the line moves below roughly 20% for 9z, the framework says the price no longer pays and the pick should follow the update on picks.html instead.

day_three_guidance.headline: Day-three guidance: contrarian, not stupid
day_three_guidance.summary: One rule decides each row: back the board favourite unless a sourced factor gives the underdog a real path and the price still leaves room. A lean is a near coin-flip that costs little; a swing is a 20-40% underdog that can move you up the leaderboard but loses more often than it wins. Percentages are read from the latest refresh at build time; the reasoning is fixed and sourced.

fixtures.label: Ninjas in Pyjamas vs Team Liquid
fixtures.why: A near coin-flip where the favourite carries a sourced cost: NIP lost both TWC series in Malta and return to Sweden with less than 24 hours before this quarter-final. While the market and our model stay near 50/50, backing Liquid costs only a few hundredths of a point in expected value and separates you from everyone who follows the bigger name.

fixtures.label: Aurora vs 9z
fixtures.verdict: The day's contrarian swing: only if you need ground
fixtures.why: 9z beat Aurora 2-0 on day one (Inferno 13-11, Nuke 13-1 on Aurora's own pick) and took a map off Falcons, so a 9z pick is not stupid. But the market and our VRS model already price the rematch at roughly 2-to-1 for Aurora, Aurora beat 9z 2-0 in the EPL 24 opener on 3 October, and Aurora looked sharp against NIP. Take 9z only if you need to gain ground.

fixtures.label: Voca vs Phantom
fixtures.why: The exchange favours Phantom, while Valve's standings rate Voca higher (1182 vs 1147 points), so our VRS model makes Voca a slight favourite. When the market and an independent rating disagree on the favourite, the underdog side is a reasonable contrarian pick.

not_listed.label: BETBOOM vs Legacy
not_listed.timing: HLTV lists it three hours after Aurora vs 9z, whose 14:00 UTC start is machine-verified, so about 17:00 UTC (derived, unverified until Hotspawn lists it).
not_listed.why: Not in Hotspawn's CS2 feed at the last capture, so it has no pick on the board; if Hotspawn lists it, the refresh prices it automatically. On ratings Legacy are clear favourites, but the contrarian case for BETBOOM is real: arT's return from meningitis ('aim still a bit shaky'), Legacy's day-two loss to FURIA, and BETBOOM's Major-qualification stakes. Consider BETBOOM only if they are still priced at 25% or better.

unverified: BETBOOM vs Legacy start time is derived from HLTV's relative schedule, not from a machine-readable timestamp or Hotspawn.
Hotspawn crowd pick shares are deliberately not used, so 'contrarian' means against the market favourite, not against measured crowd behaviour.
Fatigue and rust are sourced factors, not measured effects; they justify a pick in a near coin-flip, never against a heavy favourite.
